title: SLO experimentation and soft-capacity rollback guide
author: Leah Chen
body:
Summary
This runbook describes a controlled process for A/B-style SLO experiments (soft change to SLO thresholds or traffic allocation) combined with a low-friction "soft-capacity" rollback path. It is intended for service owners and SREs running capacity-constrained inference services (examples: inference-gateway, emb-encoder, realtime-chat). The goal is to let product/ML teams experiment with more aggressive throughput or model variants while preserving customer-facing SLOs and ensuring quick, observable rollback when risk signals appear.

Why this exists
- SLOs must be both guardrails and learning mechanisms; safe experiments accelerate cost/perf optimization.
- Traditional hard cutovers are too risky for multi-tenant LLM inference.
- Soft-capacity rollback provides an intermediate safety layer (capacity and routing controls that can be quickly tightened without code deploy).

Audience and ownership
- Primary: service owners (Product/ML + SRE oncall)
- Secondary: Platform/Infra owners who operate autoscalers and regional routing
- Ownership: service owner owns experiment plan; SRE owns observability triggers and rollback authority

Applicability
- Use for: model variant rollouts, quantization profile changes, trial autoscale policy relaxations, tenant burst tests
- Do NOT use for: security fixes, data residency changes, or experiments that alter persisted user data semantics

Experiment pre-flight checklist (must pass before enabling any soft experiment)
1) Rollout plan and hypothesis (one paragraph): what will change; expected SLO impact; success metrics.
2) Runbook fill: link to this doc and the service runbook.
3) Stakeholder sign-offs: product, SRE, infra (email or Slack thread).
4) Canary window defined: start_time, duration, target tenant(s), traffic fraction.
5) Telemetry readiness verified: Prometheus metrics, synthetic canary, distributed tracing, and cost meter.
6) Backstop capacity knobs identified and tested in staging.

Example experiment metadata (table)
| field | example |
|---|---|
| service | inference-gateway |
| owner | inference-team@redwood.com |
| change | move model-v2 quantized -> INT8; reduce per-request memory fingerprinting |
| canary tenants | tenant-demo, tenant-qa |
| fraction | 5% traffic for 2 hours |
| expected delta | p95 latency +10ms, token cost -22% |
| abort criteria | >1.0% additional 5m error rate or p99 latency +100ms |

Instrumentation & telemetry (required)
- Metrics (Prometheus):
  - infra_slo_success_rate{service=~"inference-.*",slo="availability"}  // aggregate success rate used for SLO calculation
  - request_latency_seconds_bucket{le="0.2",service="inference-gateway"}  // compute p95/p99
  - inference_model_error_total{model_variant!=""}  // model inference errors (invalid outputs / OOMs)
- Synthetic canary: round-trip against a deterministic prompt every 30s; compare tokens/latency/semantic sanity score
- Trace sampling: 100% for canary tenants, 1% for global baseline during experiment
- Cost telemetry: per-request token cost exported to billing pipeline for trial accounting

PromQL snippets (copy/paste)
- 5m rolling SLO burn (invocation success rate for last 5m):
  
  (sum(rate(infra_slo_success_rate{service="inference-gateway",slo="availability"}[5m])) / sum(rate(infra_slo_total{service="inference-gateway",slo="availability"}[5m]))) * 100

- Canary p95 latency (60m window):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket{service="inference-gateway",tenant=~"tenant-demo|tenant-qa"}[5m])) by (le))

Risk signals and thresholds (triggers that must be monitored)
- Immediate abort (hard rollback):
  - SLO success rate for service drops by >1.0 percentage point relative to baseline over a 5m window (e.g., from 99.95% -> 98.95%)
  - p99 latency increases by >150ms sustained for 10m
  - Model error rate (inference_model_error_total) increases >300% relative to baseline over 10m
  - Autoscaler thrash: >3 scale events/min sustained for 5m
- Soft rollback (throttle/reroute first, full rollback if unresolved):
  - SLO burn rate accelerating: burn_rate_5m > 2x burn_rate_1h
  - Tenant complaint: exception to automated signal; verified by SRE via tracing

Decision matrix (operator quick reference)
1) Minor blip (single spike <10m, resolves): continue monitoring, document in experiment log.
2) Risk threshold met (one Immediate abort criterion): initiate hard rollback procedure (Section: Hard rollback).
3) Burn acceleration without immediate abort: perform soft rollback: throttle experiment fraction by 50% and enable regional fallback pool. If risk not reduced in 10m → hard rollback.

Soft rollback procedure (fast, non-deploy)
1) Oncall SRE posts to #sre-experiments with subject: "Soft-rollback: <service> <experiment-id>" and tags stakeholders.
2) Reduce canary traffic fraction via router API:
   - Example HTTP request (gateway-router):
     curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN' \
       https://router.internal.redwood/api/v1/experiment/scale \
       -d '{"experiment_id":"exp-2026-42","fraction":0.025}'
3) Activate regional fallback pool (reserve nodes):
   - kubectl scale deployment/fallback-pool -n inference --replicas=6
4) Increase synthetic cadence from 30s -> 10s for more frequent sampling (via canary-config map).
5) Monitor 5m SLO burn and p99 for 10 minutes. If stable, keep reduced fraction and open a postmortem to investigate.

Hard rollback procedure (when immediate abort criteria met)
1) Announce incident on #sre-major with context and action: "Hard rollback initiated for <service> <experiment-id>".
2) Execute rollback knobs (order matters; aim for minimal customer impact):
   a) Re-route all canary tenants to stable model variant: router API set mapping: model-v1 for tenants [tenant-demo, tenant-qa, buyer-prod-test]
   b) Revert autoscaler policy to conservative profile: POST /infra/autoscaler/policies/inference-gateway/revert
   c) Disable model-v2 in model-catalog: curl -X PATCH ... {"enabled":false} (internal model registry API)
3) Confirm rollback success by verifying:
   - infra_slo_success_rate recovers to within 0.1 percentage points of baseline within 15m
   - p99 latency drops to baseline within 20m
4) Close the incident channel only after stability validated for 30m; open a follow-up incident review.

Post-experiment analysis (15–30 day lens)
- Required artifacts: experiment hypothesis, telemetry snapshot, decision timeline (who did what and why), cost delta analysis, and remediation actions.
- Metrics to collect: SLO burn windows (5m/1h/24h), cost-per-1000-requests, model error taxonomy, scaling events timeline, tenant impact list.
- Deliverable: one-page findings + recommended next steps (roll forward, rollback permanently, or iterate).

Operational tooling checklist (automation candidates)
- Router API feature: fine-grained fractional routing by tenant and region (must support sub-1% fractions).
- Canary config templating: change cadence, buckets, and synthetic test definitions via GitOps (kustomize overlay).
- SLO burn automated alert with suggested action buttons (soft rollback, throttle 50%, hard rollback).
- Chaos simulation harness to replay production canary traces in staging against proposed changes.

Example kustomize overlay snippet (canary fraction):
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: experiment-config
data:
  experiment-id: "exp-2026-42"
  fraction: "0.05"
  canary-tenants: "tenant-demo,tenant-qa"

Rollback bake plan (to reduce operator risk)
- Always keep a small, warm fallback fleet (10% of max capacity) in each region for rapid absorption.
- Maintain an autoscaler conservative baseline profile that can be re-applied via API in <60s.
- Circulate and rehearse this guide in quarterly chaos drills.

Communication and SLO governance
- SRE has veto authority for experiment continuation if any Immediate abort criterion is met.
- Product/ML may request an exception only with written justification and an expanded rollback runway.
- All experiments must be logged in the SLO Experiment Registry (simple CSV stored in /shared/slo-experiments with columns: id, service, owner, start, end, status, notes).

Incident review template for experiments
- Title: Experiment <id> — <service> — <date>
- Summary of actions taken (timeline format)
- Telemetry evidence (links to Grafana dashboards + PromQL used)
- Root cause hypothesis and detection gap analysis
- Remediation and detection improvements (owner + due date)
- Lessons learned and next steps (iterate / roll-forward / abandon)

Training and drills
- Quarterly table-top involving SRE, product, infra to play through rollback scenarios for at least two critical services.
- Annual live drill: run a benign experiment in staging mirroring production traffic profile and practice soft/hard rollback flows.

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Router API: https://router.internal.redwood/docs#experiment-scale
- Model registry: https://models.internal.redwood/dashboard
- Sample PromQL dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/inference/slo-experiment-playback
- SLO Experiment Registry CSV path: s3://redwood-docs/slo-experiments/registry.csv
